newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN officials to visit Burma for entry talks.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN officials to visit Burma for entry talks.

text.p: A senior delegation from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) will visit Burma on Saturday to look into its preparations for entry into the seven-nation group, an ASEAN statement said on Friday.
ASEAN Secretary-General Ajit Singh and three senior staff members would visit Burma from November 2-9 at the invitation of Burmese Foreign Minister Ohn Gyaw, the statement said.

"During his visit, the Secretary-General will hold discussions with the Myanmarese (Burmese) foreign minister and other Myanmarese leaders. The purpose of the visit is to look into preparations necessary for Myanmar's entry into ASEAN," the statement said.

Ohn Gyaw said on Friday he was confident Burma would be accepted as a full member. "By virtue of the fact that you have observer status it is just a matter of time, sooner or later you will be integrated into ASEAN," Ohn Gyaw told a monthly news conference in Rangoon.
Burma was accorded observer status at the 29th ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Jakarta in July and attended the Third ASEAN Regional Forum held in conjunction with the meeting.

Rangoon subsequently applied for ASEAN membership and expressed the hope it could join as early as next year despite international concerns about its human rights record and repression of the democracy movement led by Nobel laureate Aung Sang Suu Kyi.

Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, who leads a country with heavy investments in Burma and a cautious foreign policy, told Finnish television on Thursday he did not think Burma was ready for membership on economic grounds.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Laos and Cambodia are due to join next year.
The bloc has maintained a policy of "constructive engagement" with Burma's military rulers on the grounds such contacts would spark reform within the country.
But this has come under fire from human rights activists who argue Burmese membership of ASEAN would amount to approval of the ruling military State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
SLORC refused to recognise a 1990 election which was won by the National League for Democracy party led by Suu Kyi, daughter of revered independence hero Aung San.
The United States and the European Union have both imposed travel limitations on senior Burmese officials and some Western business interests also launched boycotts of Burmese businesses.
